level.description: The level of the course (e.g., CBSE, ICSE, WBBSE, WBCHSE).

tutorId.description: Reference to the Tutor offering this course. (Relationship: Tutor 1:N Course)

Tutor.title: Tutor
Tutor.description: Represents a tutor at BioMyDream Academy.

qualifications.description: The qualifications of the tutor (e.g., B.Sc., M.Sc., B.Ed., D.El.Ed.).

teachingFields.description: The teaching fields of the tutor (e.g., Science & Math, Biology).

Student.title: Student
Student.description: Represents a student at BioMyDream Academy.

email.description: The email address of the student.

courseIds.description: References to Courses the student is enrolled in. (Relationship: Student N:N Course)

Feedback.title: Feedback
Feedback.description: Represents feedback given by a student for a course.

id.description: Unique identifier for the feedback entry.

studentId.description: Reference to the Student who provided the feedback. (Relationship: Student 1:N Feedback)

courseId.description: Reference to the Course the feedback is about. (Relationship: Course 1:N Feedback)

rating.description: The rating given by the student (e.g., 1-5).

comment.description: The comment provided by the student.

date.description: The date the feedback was submitted.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to accommodate the entities and relationships described in the input, focusing on authorization independence, clarity, and scalability. User-owned data and collaborative data patterns have been applied where relevant.

*   **Authorization Independence:** The `Feedback` subcollection under `/courses/{courseId}` includes the `studentId` field in each document. This denormalization strategy makes it possible to write security rules for feedback based solely on the feedback document and the current user's authentication state, without needing to read the parent `Course` or `Student` document.

*   **Structural Segregation:** Each collection is designed to contain documents with a homogeneous security posture.

*   **Access Modeling:**
    *   The `/users/{userId}/` path pattern enforces path-based ownership for student-related data.
    *   The `/courses/{courseId}/feedbacks/{feedbackId}` path creates a hierarchical structure.

*   **QAPs (Rules Are Not Filters):** The structure enables secure list operations. For instance, listing feedbacks for a course is constrained by the security rules applied to `/courses/{courseId}/feedbacks`. Because `studentId` is stored in each `Feedback` document, rules can easily filter based on the requesting user's ID without needing complex queries or risking insecure data exposure.

The design prioritizes ease of understanding and maintainability for security rules.
